name: [Portal] CORS & build-time API token for partners_web (BE)
description:
### Summary

`partners_web`'s `HttpApi` (`DATA_SOURCE=http`) calls the real API at build time with an optional `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>`, and — per CZ3TDR1-682's technical notes — `cms/packages/Cors/Helper/CorsHeaders.php` today only allow-lists `SHOPTET_PARTNERS_CZ`. Once CZ3TDR1-722 exists, it needs to actually be reachable from the `partners_web` build (and later, SK/HU instances or a static host).

### Why?

An API nobody can reach isn't "connected functional data" — this is the last wiring step between CZ3TDR1-722 and a real `partners_web` build.

### What?

Issue/rotate the service token `partners_web`'s build pipeline uses, wire it into whatever auth check CZ3TDR1-722 implements for its `bearerAuth` scheme, and extend the CORS allow-list for any origins that call the API from the browser (the reCAPTCHA-protected form POSTs are browser calls; the GET endpoints are build-time server calls and don't strictly need CORS — confirm against how `partners_web`'s `client.ts` posts forms).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Build-time bearer token issued and documented (where it's stored/rotated); CZ3TDR1-722's GET endpoints reject requests without it
- [ ] Form POST endpoints (from CZ3TDR1-718, CZ3TDR1-719, CZ3TDR1-721) confirmed public (`security: []`) and reachable cross-origin from `partneri.shoptet.cz`'s browser context; CORS allow-list updated if currently blocked
- [ ] `cms/packages/Statistics/Helper/InternalStatsHelper.php`'s dependency on the WordPress `wp-json/post-count-api/v2/count` endpoint rewired to read from CZ3TDR1-722 (or explicitly deferred to CZ3TDR1-682's cutover, if cleaner) — don't leave it silently broken once WordPress is decommissioned
- [ ] Smoke test: a build of `partners_web` with `DATA_SOURCE=http`, `API_URL`, `API_TOKEN` pointed at a local/staging cms4 succeeds end-to-end

### Resources

- Epic: CZ3TDR1-614
- Depends on: CZ3TDR1-722
- Related: CZ3TDR1-682
